title: Asking what one thing is
summary: Build the bounded question Mikä tämä on? and its tuo and se counterparts.
objectives: Begin a singular identity question with mikä.
Place the supplied demonstrative phrase before on.
End the complete question with a question mark.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: Use Mikä ... on? to ask what one identified referent is.
The question word comes first and the singular olla form on comes last.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: The demonstrative may stand alone or begin a supplied noun phrase.
This lesson teaches only the bounded singular identity frame.

steps: tämä esine: the complete phrase is supplied.
tuo esine: the complete phrase is supplied.
se esine: the complete phrase is supplied.

commonMistakes: Do not begin this identity question with mitä.
Do not omit the final on.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Choose the sentence that means “What is the building?” Use se (“that or it, already identifiable”), rakennus (“building”), and on (“is”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Mikä ... on asks what one thing is. In English, begin with “What is” before the subject.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question word + demonstrative noun phrase + linking verb at the end of the question

parts.role: linking verb at the end of the question

optionFeedback.Mikä se rakennus on?: Correct. The singular identity frame begins with Mikä and ends with on.
optionFeedback.Mitä se rakennus on?: “Mitä” is the plural classification-question word used in this bounded frame; use “Mikä”, the singular identity-question word used in this bounded frame.
optionFeedback.Se rakennus on?: “Se” is a singular nominative form for an already identifiable non-human referent; use “Mikä”, the singular identity-question word used in this bounded frame.
optionFeedback.Mikä se rakennus ovat?: “ovat” is the plural affirmative form of olla; use “on”, the singular affirmative form of olla.
